Screenshot a .tsx component (or a ui() task) to PNG from the command line
entries.source:
# One-time per machine (add --with-deps on a fresh Linux server):
e3-ui install-browser

# A .tsx exporting an East function returning UIComponentType, or an e3 ui() task:
e3-ui shot --from-source ./dashboard.tsx -o dashboard.png

# Pick an export, set a viewport, also emit standalone HTML:
e3-ui shot --from-source src/ui/index.tsx --export surface --viewport 800x600 --html

entries.test: Sweep a project for every renderable UI export (fns, example() defs, ui() tasks) and render each to a structured .shots/ dir
entries.source:
# EVERYTHING renderable under src/ (default) → .shots/<relative-path>/<export>.png
# One shared browser; every skip carries its typed reason; exit 1 on render failures.
e3-ui shots src --out .shots --json

# Also write a standalone HTML beside each PNG:
e3-ui shots src --out .shots --html

# Width-flexible components (Schematic/Plan/Table) mount at viewport width by
# default (--frame-width full); 'none' restores the shrink-to-fit crop:
e3-ui shots test/collections --out .shots --frame-width full

# Skips are an AUDIT of the renderable surface — e.g.:
#   skipped  src/tasks.ts › sumExample — output type is Integer, not UIComponentType
#   skipped  src/ui/queue.tsx › queuePage — reads e3 workspace data (data_read) — use --from-task

Open an e3 repository in the terminal — a local path, a remote repository, or a bare origin
entries.source:
# The terminal UI is the default command (no browser needed):
e3-ui                                    # $E3_REPO, then the current directory
e3-ui ./my-repo main                     # a workspace's dashboard: task/dataset status, the last or live run, tasks + inputs
e3-ui ./my-repo main --task forecast     # straight to a task (1 Output · 2 Logs · 3 Runs); --input <name> opens an input
e3-ui https://e3.example.com/repos/demo  # remote — after: e3-ui auth login https://e3.example.com
e3-ui https://e3.example.com             # a bare origin: the repositories list
e3-ui --no-mouse --ascii ./my-repo       # keyboard only, box-drawing off

# Without a TTY (a script, CI) it refuses with exit 1 — use the scriptable commands:
e3 workspace status ./my-repo main
e3 dataset get ./my-repo main.forecast -f json

entries.test: Drive the terminal UI: the command box, the fuzzy jump, the keys, and the mouse
entries.source:
# / opens the command box (Tab completes, ⏎ runs, esc cancels); plain text fuzzy-jumps anywhere.
/task forecast        /input params        /workspace staging        /repo https://host/repos/x
/run --force          /run --filter fore* --jobs 2               /stop        (r and x prefill them)
/logs forecast stderr /runs forecast
/find "k0150"         /find k015 (prefix)   /find Bakery|2025-09 (struct-key fields)   /goto 620000   /goto 50%
/save                 (writes <ws>.<name>.beast2 — or <ws>.<task>.<stream>.log on the Logs tab; --force overwrites)
/tag monthly          /add region          /remove          /apply          /discard          (editing an input)
/refresh              /help                /about           /quit

# Keys: ↑↓ j k move · pgup pgdn ^u ^d · gg G · ⏎ → open · esc ⌫ back · 1 2 3 4 tabs · ? help · q quit
#   value tree: → l expand-or-next · ← h collapse-or-parent · ⏎ space toggle · ⇧← collapse deep · n N next/prev match · s save
#   logs:       ↑↓ scroll (pauses follow) · G end · F follow · o e stdout/stderr · s save · c copy (OSC 52)
#   inputs:     e edit · a add · x remove · t tag/set · ⏎ apply all · esc discard (in an editor: ⏎ commit · esc cancel · space toggles a boolean)
#   mouse:      wheel scrolls the pane under the cursor · click selects (on ▸ toggles) · drag the scrollbar thumb · click tabs / crumbs / pills

entries.test: Sign in to a remote e3 server for the terminal UI — the same device flow and credential store as e3 auth
entries.source:
# The same commands, device flow and store (~/.e3/credentials.json, E3_CREDENTIALS_PATH) as `e3 auth`:
e3-ui auth login https://e3.example.com     # prints a code + URL, waits, saves the token
e3-ui auth status                            # every saved server
e3-ui auth whoami https://e3.example.com     # the signed-in identity
e3-ui auth token https://e3.example.com      # a valid access token (refreshed if needed) for curl / scripts
e3-ui auth logout https://e3.example.com

# Then open a repository there (the token is re-resolved per request, so long sessions survive expiry):
e3-ui https://e3.example.com/repos/demo
# Inside the UI, /login <url> runs the same device flow without leaving it.

entries.test: Scaffold a new e3 project (durable dataflow; Node + Python + C runners)
entries.source:
# Interactive when a TTY; pass flags after `--` for a non-interactive run:
npm create @elaraai/e3 my-app
npm create @elaraai/e3 .                       # scaffold into the current directory
npm create @elaraai/e3 my-app -- --no-ui --install

entries.test: Choose which East runtimes a project includes (default: all three)
entries.source:
# Default is east-node,east-py,east-c; prune to what you need (drops unused setup):
npm create @elaraai/e3 planner -- --runners=east-node,east-py

entries.test: Split platform code into per-runtime workspace packages for per-package change detection
entries.source:
# Each package is its own captured environment — editing one re-runs only its tasks:
npm create @elaraai/e3 my-app -- --python-packages=pricing --node-packages=api --c-packages=solver
# generates packages/python/pricing (uv member), packages/node/api (npm member),
# packages/native/solver (tools env) + src/packages/{pricing,api,solver}.ts wiring each
# task to its runner. python/node auto-derive the env from { custom }; C attaches the binary.
